metadata.title: A $(p,\nu)$-extension of Srivastava's triple hypergeometric function $H_B$ and its properties

nodes.name: Srivastava's triple hypergeometric function $H_{B}$
nodes.statement: In the present study, we confine our attention to Srivastava's triple hypergeometric function $H_{B}$ given by \cite[p. 43, 1.5(11) to 1.5(13)]{AB37} (see also \cite{AB34} and \cite[p.~68]{AB36}) \[ H_{B}(b_{1},b_{2},b_{3};c_{1},c_{2},c_{3};x,y,z) :=\sum_{m,n,k=0}^{\infty}\frac{(b_{1})_{m+k}(b_{2})_{m+n}(b_{3})_{n+k}}{(c_{1})_{m}(c_{2})_{n}(c_{3})_{k}} \frac{x^{m}}{m!}\frac{y^{n}}{n!}\frac{z^{k}}{k!}\] \bee =\sum_{m,n,k=0}^{\infty}\frac{(b_{1}\!+\!b_2)_{2m+n+k}(b_{3})_{n+k}}{(c_{1})_{m}(c_{2})_{n}(c_{3})_{k}}\,\frac{B(b_1\!+\!m\!+\!k,b_2\!+\!m\!+\!n)}{B(b_1,b_2)}\, \frac{x^{m}}{m!}\frac{y^{n}}{n!}\frac{z^{k}}{k!}. \ee
nodes.statement_short: Srivastava's $H_B$ is the triple series with Pochhammer factors $(b_1)_{m+k}(b_2)_{m+n}(b_3)_{n+k}$, equivalently written with a ratio of classical Beta functions.

nodes.name: Pochhammer symbol (shifted factorial) $(\lambda)_n$
nodes.statement: Here $(\lambda)_{n}$ denotes the Pochhammer symbol (or the shifted factorial, since $(1)_{n}=n!)$ defined by \[ (\lambda)_n:=\frac{\Gamma(\lambda+n)}{\Gamma(\lambda)}=\left\{\begin{array}{ll}1, & (n=0,\ \lambda\in{\bf C}\backslash\{0\})\\ \lambda(\lambda+1)...(\lambda+n-1), & (n\in{\bf N},~\lambda\in{\bf C}) \end{array}\right. \]
nodes.statement_short: $(\lambda)_n=\Gamma(\lambda+n)/\Gamma(\lambda)$, equal to $1$ for $n=0$ and to the rising product $\lambda(\lambda+1)\cdots(\lambda+n-1)$ otherwise.

nodes.name: classical Beta function $B(\alpha,\beta)$
nodes.statement: and $B(\alpha, \beta)$ denotes the classical Beta function defined by \cite[(5.12.1)]{AB26} \begin{equation} B(\alpha, \beta)=\left\{\begin{array}{ll} \displaystyle{\int_{0}^{1}t^{\alpha-1}(1-t)^{\beta-1}dt}, & (\Re(\alpha)>0, \Re(\beta)>0)\\ \\ \displaystyle{\frac{\Gamma(\alpha)\Gamma(\beta)}{\Gamma(\alpha+\beta)}}, & ( (\alpha,\beta)\in{\bf C}\backslash {\bf Z}_{0}^{-}). \end{array}\right. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: The Beta function is the Euler integral $\int_0^1 t^{\alpha-1}(1-t)^{\beta-1}dt$ for $\Re\alpha,\Re\beta>0$, and $\Gamma(\alpha)\Gamma(\beta)/\Gamma(\alpha+\beta)$ in general.

nodes.name: Exton's triple hypergeometric function $X_{4}$
nodes.statement: A different type of triple hypergeometric function is Exton's function $ X_{4}(\cdot)$, which is defined by (see \cite{AB19} and \cite[p.~84, Entry (45a)]{AB37}) \begin{equation} X_{4}(b_{1},b_{2};c_{1},c_{2},c_{3};x,y,z):=\sum_{m,n,k=0}^{\infty}\frac{(b_{1})_{2m+n+k}(b_{2})_{n+k}}{(c_{1})_{m}(c_{2})_{n}(c_{3})_{k}} \frac{x^{m}}{m!}\frac{y^{n}}{n!}\frac{z^{k}}{k!}. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Exton's $X_4$ is the triple series with numerator Pochhammer factors $(b_1)_{2m+n+k}(b_2)_{n+k}$.

nodes.name: $H_{B}^{(a)}$, the $H_B$ series with an additional parameter $a$
nodes.statement: We shall also find it convenient to introduce an additional parameter $a$ into $H_B(\cdot)$ in the form \[H_{B}^{(a)}(b_{1},b_{2},b_{3};c_{1},c_{2},c_{3};x,y,z):=\hspace{6cm}\] \bee \sum_{m,n,k=0}^{\infty}\frac{(b_{1}\!+\!b_2)_{2m+n+k}(b_{3})_{n+k}}{(c_{1})_{m}(c_{2})_{n}(c_{3})_{k}}\,\frac{B(b_1\!+\!a\!+\!m\!+\!k,b_2\!+\!a\!+\!m\!+\!n)}{B(b_1,b_2)}\, \frac{x^{m}}{m!}\frac{y^{n}}{n!}\frac{z^{k}}{k!}, \ee which reduces to (\ref{PV2}) when $a=0$.
nodes.statement_short: $H_B^{(a)}$ shifts both Beta arguments of $H_B$ by $a$, reducing to $H_B$ at $a=0$.

nodes.name: $p$-extension of the Beta function $B(x,y;p)$
nodes.statement: In 1997, Chaudhry {\it et al.} \cite[Eq.(1.7)]{AB8} gave a $p$-extension of the Beta function $B(x, y)$ given by \[B(x,y; p)= \int_0^1 t^{x-1}(1-t)^{y-1}\,\exp \left[\frac{-p}{t(1-t)}\right]dt,\qquad (\Re (p)>0)\]
nodes.statement_short: $B(x,y;p)$ inserts the exponential regulator $\exp[-p/(t(1-t))]$ into the Euler Beta integral.
nodes.definiendum: a $p$-extension of the Beta function $B(x, y)$

nodes.name: extended Beta function $B_{p,\nu}(x,y)$
nodes.statement:
Recently, Parmar {\it et al.} \cite{AB30} have given a further extension of the extended Beta function $B(x,y;p)$ by adding one more parameter $
u$, which we denote and define by  egin{equation} B_{p,
u}(x,y)=\sqrt{ rac{2p}{\pi}}\displaystyle{\int_{0}^{1}t^{x- rac{3}{2}}(1-t)^{y- rac{3}{2}}} K_{
u+ rac{1}{2}}\left( rac{p}{t(1-t)}ight)dt, \end{equation} where $\Re(p)>0$, $
u\geq0$ and $K_{
u}(z)$ is the modified Bessel function (sometimes known as the Macdonald function) of order $
u$.
nodes.statement_short: $B_{p,\nu}(x,y)$ replaces the exponential regulator of $B(x,y;p)$ by the modified Bessel kernel $K_{\nu+1/2}(p/(t(1-t)))$.

nodes.name: $(p,\nu)$-extended Srivastava triple hypergeometric function $H_{B,p,\nu}$
nodes.statement:
Here we consider the following $(p,
u)$-extension of this function, which we denote by $H_{B,p,
u}(\cdot)$, based on the extended Beta function $B_{p,
u}(x,y)$ defined in (ef{ES20}). This is given by \[H_{B,p,
u}(b_{1},b_{2},b_{3};c_{1},c_{2},c_{3};x,y,z)\]  ee =\sum_{m,n,k=0}^{\infty} rac{(b_{1}\!+\!b_{2})_{2m+n+k}(b_{3})_{n+k}}{(c_{1})_{m}(c_{2})_{n}(c_{3})_{k}} rac{B_{p,
u}(b_{1}\!+\!m\!+\!k,b_{2}\!+\!m\!+\!n)} {B(b_{1},b_{2})}  rac{x^{m}}{m!} rac{y^{n}}{n!} rac{z^{k}}{k!}, \ee where the parameters $b_{1},b_{2},b_{3}\in{ f C}$ and $c_{1},c_{2}, c_{2}\in{ f C} ackslash { f Z}_{0}^{-}$. The region of convergence is $|x|<r$, $|y|<s$, $|z|<t$, where $r+s+t+2\sqrt{rst}=1$.
nodes.statement_short: $H_{B,p,\nu}$ is $H_B$ with the classical Beta numerator replaced by the extended Beta function $B_{p,\nu}$.

nodes.name: Mellin transform
nodes.statement: The Mellin transform of a locally integrable function $f(x)$ on $(0,\infty)$ is given by (see, for example, \cite[p.193, Section 2.1]{AB125}) \begin{equation} \Phi(s)={\cal M}\left\{f(x)\right\}(s)=\int_{0}^{\infty}x^{s-1}f(x)\,dx \end{equation} which defines an analytic function in its strip of analyticity $a<\Re (s)<b$.
nodes.statement_short: $\Phi(s)=\int_0^\infty x^{s-1}f(x)dx$, analytic in a vertical strip $a<\Re(s)<b$.

nodes.name: inverse Mellin transform
nodes.statement: The inverse Mellin transform of the above function (\ref{PV27}) is defined by \begin{equation} f(x)={\cal M}^{-1}\left\{\Phi(s)\right\}=\frac{1}{2\pi i}\int_{c-i\infty}^{c+i\infty}x^{-s}\Phi(s)\,ds \qquad (a<c<b). \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: $f(x)=\frac{1}{2\pi i}\int_{c-i\infty}^{c+i\infty}x^{-s}\Phi(s)ds$ on a vertical line inside the strip.

nodes.name: Integral representations of $H_{B,p,\nu}$ in terms of Exton's function $X_4$
nodes.statement_short: Five equivalent single-integral representations of $H_{B,p,\nu}$ with a Bessel kernel $K_{\nu+1/2}$ against Exton's $X_4$, over $[0,1]$, $[\alpha,\beta]$ and three trigonometric contours.
conclusions: H_{B,p,\nu}(b_{1},b_{2},b_{3};c_{1},c_{2},c_{3};x,y,z)=\frac{(\beta-\gamma)^{b_{1}-\frac{1}{2}}(\alpha-\gamma)^{b_{2}-\frac{1}{2}}}{(\beta-\alpha)^{b_{1}+b_{2}-2}} \frac{\Gamma(b_{1}+b_{2})}{\Gamma(b_{1})\Gamma(b_{2})}\sqrt{\frac{2p}{\pi}}\] \bee \times\int_{\alpha}^{\beta}\frac{(\xi-\alpha)^{b_{1}-\frac{3}{2}}(\beta-\xi)^{b_{2}-\frac{3}{2}}}{(\xi-\gamma)^{b_{1}+b_{2}-1}} K_{\nu+\frac{1}{2}}\left(\frac{p}{\sigma_1 \sigma_2}\right) X_{4}( b_{1}+b_{2},b_{3};c_{1},c_{2},c_{3}; \sigma_1\sigma_2 x,\sigma_1 y, \sigma_2 z)\,d\xi, \ee where \[\sigma_{1}=\frac{(\alpha-\gamma)(\beta-\xi)}{(\beta-\alpha)(\xi-\gamma)},\qquad \sigma_{2}=\frac{(\beta-\gamma)(\xi-\alpha)}{(\beta-\alpha)(\xi-\gamma)}\quad (\gamma<\alpha<\beta);

nodes.name: Mellin transform of $H_{B,p,\nu}$
nodes.statement:
The following Mellin transform of the extended Srivastava triple hypergeometric function $ H_{B,p,
u}(\cdot)$ holds true: \[ {\cal M}\left\{H_{B,p,
u}(b_{1},b_{2},b_{3};c_{1},c_{2},c_{3};x,y,z)ight\}(s)=\int_{0}^{\infty}p^{s-1} H_{B,p,
u}(b_{1},b_{2},b_{3};c_{1},c_{2},c_{3};x,y,z)\,dp,\]  egin{equation} = rac{2^{s-1}}{\sqrt{\pi}}\Gamma\left( rac{s-
u}{2}ight)\Gamma\left( rac{s+
u+1}{2}ight) H_{B}^{(s)}\left(b_{1},b_{2},b_{3};c_{1},c_{2},c_{3};x,y,zight), \end{equation} where $\Re\,(s)>
u>0$, $c_{1},c_{2},c_{3}\in{ f C} ackslash{ f Z}_{0}^{-}$ and $H_B^{(s)}(\cdot)$ is defined in (ef{PV2a}).
nodes.statement_short:
The Mellin transform in $p$ of $H_{B,p,
u}$ equals $2^{s-1}\pi^{-1/2}\Gamma( rac{s-
u}{2})\Gamma( rac{s+
u+1}{2})$ times the shifted function $H_B^{(s)}$.

nodes.name: Differentiation formula for $H_{B,p,\nu}$
nodes.statement:
The following derivative formula for $H_{B,p,
u}(\cdot)$ holds: \[ rac{\partial^{M+N+K}}{\partial x^{M}\partial y^{N}\partial z^{K}}~H_{B,p,
u}\left(b_{1},b_{2},b_{3};c_{1},c_{2},c_{3};x,y,zight) = rac{(b_{1})_{M+K}(b_{2})_{M+N}(b_{3})_{N+K}}{(c_{1})_{M}(c_{2})_{N}(c_{3})_{K}}\]  ee 	imes H_{B,p,
u}(b_{1}\!+\!M\!+\!K,b_{2}\!+\!M\!+\!N,b_{3}\!+\!N\!+\!K;c_{1}\!+\!M,c_{2}\!+\!N, c_{3}\!+\!K;x,y,z), \ee where $M$, $N$, $K\in{ f N}_{0}$.
nodes.statement_short: Mixed partial derivatives of order $(M,N,K)$ in $x,y,z$ reproduce $H_{B,p,\nu}$ with all parameters shifted, times a Pochhammer prefactor.

nodes.name: Bounded inequality for $H_{B,p,\nu}$
nodes.statement:
Let the parameters $b_j$, $c_j$ $(1\leq j\leq 3)$ be positive and the variables $x$, $y$, $z$ be complex. Then the following bounded inequality for $H_{B,p,
u}(\cdot)$ holds: \[|H_{B,p,
u}(b_{1},b_{2},b_{3};c_{1},c_2,c_3;x,y,z)|\hspace{8cm}\]  ee < rac{2^
u |p|^{
u+1}}{\sqrt{\pi} (\Re (p))^{2
u+1}}\,\Gamma(
u+ s)\,H_B^{(
u)}(b_1,b_2,b_3;c_1,c_2,c_3;|x|,|y|,|z|), \ee where $\Re(p)>0$, $
u>0$ and $H_B^{(
u)}(\cdot)$ is defined in (ef{PV2a})
nodes.statement_short:
$|H_{B,p,
u}|$ is bounded by $2^
u|p|^{
u+1}(\Re p)^{-2
u-1}\pi^{-1/2}\Gamma(
u+ rac12)$ times $H_B^{(
u)}$ evaluated at $|x|,|y|,|z|$.
assumptions: Let the parameters $b_j$, $c_j$ $(1\leq j\leq 3)$ be positive and the variables $x$, $y$, $z$ be complex.

nodes.name: Recursion for $H_{B,p,\nu}$ in the numerator parameter $b_3$
nodes.statement:
The following recursion for $H_{B,p,
u}(\cdot)$ with respect to the numerator parameter $b_3$ holds: \[H_{B,p,
u}(b_1,b_2,b_3\!+\!1;c_1,c_2,c_3;x,y,z)=H_{B,p,
u}(b_1,b_2,b_3;c_1,c_2,c_3;x,y,z)\]  ee + rac{yb_2}{c_2} H_{B,p,
u}(b_1,b_2\!+\!1,b_3\!+\!1;c_1, c_2+1,c_3; x,y,z)+ rac{zb_1}{c_3} H_{B,p,
u}(b_1\!+\!1,b_2,b_3\!+\!1;c_1, c_2,c_3\!+\!1; x,y,z). \ee
nodes.statement_short: $H_{B,p,\nu}$ with $b_3\to b_3+1$ equals itself plus two shifted copies weighted by $yb_2/c_2$ and $zb_1/c_3$.
assumptions: the parameters $b_{1},b_{2},b_{3}\in{\bf C}$ and $c_{1},c_{2}, c_{2}\in{\bf C}\backslash {\bf Z}_{0}^{-}$

nodes.name: Three-term recursion for $H_{B,p,\nu}$ in the denominator parameter $c_1$
nodes.statement:
The following 3-term recursion for $H_{B,p,
u}(\cdot)$ with respect to the denominator parameter $c_1$ holds: \[H_{B,p,
u}(b_1,b_2,b_3;c_1,c_2,c_3;x,y,z)=\]  ee H_{B,p,
u}(b_1,b_2,b_3;c_1+1,c_2,c_3;x,y,z)+ rac{x b_1 b_2}{c_1(c_1+1)} H_{B,p,
u}(b_1+1,b_2+1,b_3;c_1+2,c_2,c_3;x,y,z). \ee Permutation of the $c_j$ enables analogous recursions in the denominator parameters $c_2$ and $c_3$ to be obtained.
nodes.statement_short: $H_{B,p,\nu}$ equals its $c_1\to c_1+1$ shift plus $xb_1b_2/(c_1(c_1+1))$ times the $c_1\to c_1+2$, $b_1,b_2$-shifted function; analogous relations hold for $c_2,c_3$.
assumptions: the parameters $b_{1},b_{2},b_{3}\in{\bf C}$ and $c_{1},c_{2}, c_{2}\in{\bf C}\backslash {\bf Z}_{0}^{-}$
conclusions: Permutation of the $c_j$ enables analogous recursions in the denominator parameters $c_2$ and $c_3$ to be obtained.

nodes.name: Corollary 1: inverse Mellin formula for $H_{B,p,\nu}$
nodes.statement:
The following inverse Mellin formula for $H_{B,p,
u}(\cdot)$ holds: \[H_{B,p,
u}(b_{1},b_{2},b_{3};c_{1},c_{2},c_{3};x,y,z)={\cal M}^{-1}\left\{\Phi(s)ight\}\hspace{4cm}\]  ee = rac{\pi^{-3/2}}{4i}\int_{c-i\infty}^{c+i\infty}\left( rac{2}{p}ight)^{s}\Gamma\left( rac{s\!-\!
u}{2}ight)\Gamma\left( rac{s\!+\!
u\!+\!1}{2}ight) H_{B}^{(s)}\left(b_{1},b_{2},b_{3};c_{1},c_{2},c_{3};x,y,zight)ds, \ee where $c>
u$.
nodes.statement_short: Inverting the Mellin transform recovers $H_{B,p,\nu}$ as a Mellin-Barnes integral in $s$ over $H_B^{(s)}$.

nodes.name: Corollary 2: $N$-fold recursion for $H_{B,p,\nu}$ in $b_3$
nodes.statement:
From (ef{e60}) the following recursion holds \[H_{B,p,
u}(b_1,b_2,b_3+N;c_1,c_2,c_3;x,y,z)=H_{B,p,
u}(b_1,b_2,b_3;c_1,c_2,c_3;x,y,z)\] \[+ rac{yb_2}{c_2}\sum_{\ell=1}^N H_{B,p,
u}(b_1,b_2+1,b_3+\ell;c_1,c_2+1,c_3;x,y,z)\]  ee + rac{zb_1}{c_3}\sum_{\ell=1}^NH_{B,p,
u}(b_1+1,b_2,b_3+\ell;c_1,c_2,c_3+1;x,y,z) \ee for positive integer $N$.
nodes.statement_short: Iterating the $b_3$ recursion $N$ times gives $H_{B,p,\nu}$ at $b_3+N$ as a finite sum over $\ell=1,\ldots,N$.

nodes.name: Mellin-type integral of the modified Bessel function $K_{\alpha+1/2}$
nodes.statement: \int_{0}^{\infty}w^{s-\frac{1}{2}}K_{\alpha+\frac{1}{2}}(w)dw=2^{s-\frac{3}{2}}\Gamma\left(\frac{s-\alpha}{2}\right) \Gamma\left(\frac{s+\alpha+1}{2}\right)\qquad (|\Re (\alpha)|<\Re (s))
nodes.statement_short: $\int_0^\infty w^{s-1/2}K_{\alpha+1/2}(w)dw = 2^{s-3/2}\Gamma(\frac{s-\alpha}{2})\Gamma(\frac{s+\alpha+1}{2})$.

nodes.name: Integral representation of the modified Bessel function $K_{\nu+1/2}(z)$
Bound for $|K_{\nu+1/2}(z)|$ involving the incomplete gamma function
Simplified bound for $|K_{\nu+1/2}(z)|$
Positivity of the parameters $b_j$, $c_j$
nodes.statement: For ease of presentation we shall assume that the parameters $b_j$, $c_j>0$ ($1\leq j\leq 3$).

nodes.name: Convergence region of Srivastava's $H_{B}$ series
nodes.statement: The convergence region for Srivastava's triple hypergeometric series $H_{B}(\cdot)$ is given in \cite[ p.243]{ab22} as $|x|<\alpha$, $|y|<\beta$, $|z|<\gamma$, where $\alpha$, $\beta$, $\gamma$ satisfy the relation $\alpha+\beta+\gamma+2\sqrt{\alpha\beta\gamma}=1$.
nodes.statement_short: $H_B$ converges for $|x|<\alpha,|y|<\beta,|z|<\gamma$ whenever $\alpha+\beta+\gamma+2\sqrt{\alpha\beta\gamma}=1$.

nodes.name: Convergence region of Exton's $X_4$ series
nodes.statement: The convergence region for this series is $2\sqrt{|x|}+(\sqrt{|y|}+\sqrt{|z|})^{2}<1$.

nodes.name: Reduction of $B_{p,\nu}$ to $B(x,y;p)$ at $\nu=0$
nodes.statement: When $\nu=0$, (\ref{ES20}) reduces to $B(x,y;p)$, since $K_\frac{1}{2}(z)=\sqrt{\pi/(2z)} e^{-z}$.

nodes.name: Reduction of $H_{B,p,\nu}$ to the classical function at $\nu=0$
nodes.statement: This definition clearly reduces to the original classical function when $\nu=0$.

nodes.name: Sharpness of the incomplete-gamma bound
nodes.statement: Although this bound is numerically found to be quite sharp when $z $ is real, it involves the incomplete gamma function which would make the integral for $F_{1,p,\nu}(b_{1},b_{2},b_{3};c_{1};x,y)$ difficult to bound.
nodes.statement_short: The incomplete-gamma bound is numerically sharp for real $z$ but too unwieldy to integrate.

nodes.name: Trade-off between the two Bessel bounds
nodes.statement: The bound (\ref{ES88}) is less sharp than (\ref{ES87}) but has the advantage of being easier to handle in the integral for $H_{B,p,\nu}(\cdot)$.

nodes.name: Concluding remarks
nodes.statement:
In this paper, we have introduced the $(p,
u)$-extended Srivastava triple hypergeometric function given by $H_{B,p,
u}(\cdot)$ in (ef{PV16}). We have given some integral representations of this function that involve the modified Bessel function of the second kind and Exton's triple hypergeometric function $X_4$. We have also established some properties of the function $H_{B,p,
u}(\cdot)$, namely the Mellin transform, a differential formula, a bounded inequality and some recursion relations.
nodes.statement_short: Summary: the paper introduces $H_{B,p,\nu}$ and establishes integral representations, its Mellin transform, a differentiation formula, a bound and recursions.

nodes.name: Proof of the integral representations of $H_{B,p,\nu}$
nodes.statement: The proof of the first integral representation (\ref{PV17}) follows by use of the extended beta function (\ref{ES20}) in (\ref{PV16}), a change the order of integration and summation (with uniform convergence of the integral) and, after simplification, use of Exton's triple hypergeometric function (\ref{PV3}), to obtain the right-hand side of the result (\ref{PV17}). The integral representations (\ref{PV18})-(\ref{PV23}) can be proved directly by using the following transformations \begin{eqnarray*} (\ref{PV18}):\qquad t&=&\frac{(\beta-\gamma)(\xi-\alpha)}{(\beta-\alpha)(\xi-\gamma)},\quad \frac{dt}{d\xi}=\frac{(\beta-\gamma)(\alpha-\gamma)}{(\beta-\alpha) (\xi-\gamma)^2},\\ (\ref{PV20}):\qquad t&=& \sin^2 \xi,\quad \frac{dt}{d\xi}=2\sin \xi \cos \xi\\ (\ref{PV21}):\qquad t&=&\frac{(1+\lambda)\sin^{2}\xi}{1+\lambda \sin^{2}\xi},\quad\frac{dt}{d\xi}=\frac{2(1+\lambda)\sin \xi \cos \xi}{(1+\lambda \sin^2 \xi)^2},\\ (\ref{PV23}):\qquad t&=&\frac{\lambda \sin^{2}\xi}{\cos^2{\xi}+\lambda \sin^{2}\xi},\quad \frac{dt}{d\xi}=\frac{2\lambda \sin \xi \cos \xi}{(\cos^2\xi+\lambda \sin^2\xi)^2}\\ \end{eqnarray*} in turn in (\ref{PV17}) to obtain the right-hand side of each result.
nodes.statement_short: Substitute the extended Beta integral into the series and interchange sum and integral to get the first representation; the other four follow by explicit changes of variable.

nodes.name: Proof of the Mellin transform of $H_{B,p,\nu}$
nodes.statement:
Substituting the extended Srivastava function (ef{PV16}) into the integral on the left-hand side of (ef{PV30}) and changing the order of integration (by the uniform convergence of the integral), we obtain \[{\cal M}\left\{H_{B,p,
u}(b_{1},b_{2},b_{3};c_{1},c_2,c_3;x,y,z)ight\}(s)\hspace{3cm}\] \[=\sum_{m,n,k=0}^{\infty} rac{(b_{1}+b_{2})_{2m+n+k}(b_{3})_{n+k}}{(c_{1})_{m}(c_{2})_{n}(c_{3})_{k}~B(b_{1},b_{2})} rac{x^{m}}{m!} rac{y^{n}}{n!} rac{z^{k}}{k!} \left\{\int_{0}^{\infty}p^{s-1}B_{p,
u}(b_{1}+m+k,b_{2}+m+n)\,dpight\}. \] Using the extended Beta function (ef{ES20}) then shows that \[{\cal M}\left\{H_{B,p,
u}(b_{1},b_{2},b_{3};c_{1},c_{2},c_{3};x,y,z)ight\}(s) =\sqrt{ rac{2}{\pi}}\sum_{m,n,k=0}^{\infty} rac{(b_{1}+b_{2})_{2m+n+k}(b_{3})_{n+k}}{(c_{1})_{m}(c_{2})_{n}(c_{3})_{k}~B(b_{1},b_{2})} rac{x^{m}}{m!} rac{y^{n}}{n!} rac{z^{k}}{k!}\] \[	imes\int_{0}^{1}t^{b_{1}+m+k- rac{3}{2}}(1-t)^{b_{2}+m+n- rac{3}{2}} \left\{\int_{0}^{\infty}p^{s- rac{1}{2}}K_{
u+ rac{1}{2}}\left( rac{p}{t(1-t)}ight)dpight\}dt.\] Application of the result \cite[(10.43.19)]{AB26} \[\int_{0}^{\infty}w^{s- rac{1}{2}}K_{\alpha+ rac{1}{2}}(w)dw=2^{s- rac{3}{2}}\Gamma\left( rac{s-\alpha}{2}ight) \Gamma\left( rac{s+\alpha+1}{2}ight)\qquad (|\Re (\alpha)|<\Re (s))\] followed by the substitution $w=p/(t(1-t))$ produces  egin{eqnarray*} {\cal M}\left\{H_{B,p,
u}(b_{1},b_{2},b_{3};c_{1},c_{2},c_{3};x,y,z)ight\}(s) = rac{2^{s-1}}{\sqrt{\pi}}\Gamma\left( rac{s-
u}{2}ight)\Gamma\left( rac{s+
u+1}{2}ight) 
onumber\ 	imes\sum_{m,n,k=0}^{\infty} rac{(b_{1}+b_{2})_{2m+n+k}(b_{3})_{n+k}}{(c_{1})_{m}(c_{2})_{n}(c_{3})_{k}~B(b_{1},b_{2})} rac{x^{m}}{m!} rac{y^{n}}{n!} rac{z^{k}}{k!} \left\{\int_{0}^{1}t^{b_{1}+m+k+s-1}(1-t)^{b_{2}+m+n+s-1}dtight\}. \end{eqnarray*} Evaluation of the integral in terms of the classical Beta function then finally yields  egin{eqnarray*} \Phi(s)={\cal M}\left\{H_{B,p,
u}(b_{1},b_{2},b_{3};c_{1},c_{2},c_{3};x,y,z)ight\}(s) = rac{2^{s-1}}{\sqrt{\pi}}\Gamma\left( rac{s-
u}{2}ight)\Gamma\left( rac{s+
u+1}{2}ight)\ 	imes\sum_{m,n,k=0}^{\infty} rac{(b_{1}+b_{2})_{2m+n+k}(b_{3})_{n+k}}{(c_{1})_{m}(c_{2})_{n}(c_{3})_{k}}  rac{B(b_{1}+m+k+s,b_{2}+m+n+s)}{B(b_{1},b_{2})} rac{x^{m}}{m!} rac{y^{n}}{n!} rac{z^{k}}{k!}. \end{eqnarray*} Identifying the above sum as $H_B^{(s)}(b_{1},b_{2},b_{3};c_{1},c_{2},c_{3};x,y,z)$ in (ef{PV2a}), we obtain the right-hand side of (ef{PV30}).
nodes.statement_short: Term-by-term Mellin transformation: interchange sum and integral, insert $B_{p,\nu}$, apply the known Bessel Mellin integral, then re-sum into $H_B^{(s)}$.

nodes.name: Proof of the differentiation formula
nodes.statement:
If we differentiate partially the series for ${\cal H}\equiv H_{B,p,
u}(b_{1},b_{2},b_{3};c_{1},c_{2},c_{3};x,y,z)$ in (ef{PV16}) with respect to $x$ we obtain \[ rac{\partial{\cal H}}{\partial x} =\sum_{m=1}^\infty \sum_{n,k=0}^\infty  rac{(b_1+b_2)_{2m+n+k} (b_3)_{n+k}}{(c_1)_m(c_2)_n(c_3)_k}\, rac{B_{p,
u}(b_1+m+k,b_2+m+n)}{B(b_1, b_2)}\, rac{x^{m-1}}{(m-1)!} rac{y^n}{n!}  rac{z^k}{k!}.\] Making use of the fact that  ee B(b_1,b_2)= rac{(b_1+b_2)_2}{b_1 b_2}\,B(b_1+1, b_2+1) \ee and $(\lambda)_{m+n}=(\lambda)_m(\lambda+m)_n$, we have upon setting $m 	o m+1$ \[ rac{\partial{\cal H}}{\partial x} = rac{b_1 b_2}{c_1} \sum_{m,n,k=0}^\infty  rac{(b_1+b_2+2)_{2m+n+k} (b_3)_{n+k}}{(c_1+1)_m(c_2)_n(c_3)_k}\, rac{B_{p,
u}(b_1\!+\!1\!+\!m\!+\!k,b_2\!+\!1\!+\!m\!+\!n)}{B(b_1+1, b_2+1)}\, rac{x^{m}}{m!} rac{y^n}{n!}  rac{z^k}{k!}\]  ee = rac{b_1 b_2}{c_1}\,H_{B,p,
u}(b_1+1,b_2+1,b_3;c_1+1,c_2,c_3;x,y,z). \ee Repeated application of (ef{e41}) then yields for $M=1, 2, \ldots $ \[ rac{\partial^M}{\partial x^M}{\cal H}=  rac{(b_1)_M (b_2)_M}{(c_1)_M}\,H_{B,p,
u}(b_{1}+M,b_{2}+M,b_{3};c_{1}+M,c_{2},c_{3};x,y,z).\] A similar reasoning shows that \[ rac{\partial^{M+1}}{\partial x^M \partial y}{\cal H} = rac{(b_1)_M (b_2)_M}{(c_1)_M} \sum_{m,k=0}^\infty \sum_{n=1}^\infty  rac{(b_1\!+\!b_2\!+\!2M)_{2m+n+k} (b_3)_{n+k}}{(c_1\!+\!M)_m (c_2)_n(c_3)_k}\hspace{3cm}\] \[\hspace{3cm}	imes rac{B_{p, 
u}(b_1\!+\!M\!+\!m\!+\!k,b_2\!+\!M\!+\!n\!+\!k)}{B(b_1\!+\!M, b_2\!+\!M)}\, rac{x^m}{m!}  rac{y^{n-1}}{(n-1)!} rac{z^k}{k!}\]  ee = rac{(b_1)_{M} (b_2)_{M+1} b_3}{(c_1)_{M}c_2}\,H_{B,p,
u}(b_1+M,b_2+M+1,b_3+1;c_1+M,c_2+1,c_3;x,y,z) \ee upon putting $n	o n+1$ and using the property of the Beta function in (ef{ES5}). Repeated differentiation of (ef{e42}) $N$ times with respect to $y$ then produces \[ rac{\partial^{M+N}}{\partial x^M \partial y^N} {\cal H}= rac{(b_1)_M (b_2)_{M+N} (b_3)_N}{(c_1)_M (c_2)_N}\, H_{B,p,
u}(b_1\!+\!M,b_2\!+\!M\!+\!N,b_3\!+\!N;c_1\!+\!M,c_2\!+\!N,c_3;x,y,z).\] Application of the same procedure to deal with differentiation with respect to $z$ then yields the result stated in (ef{PV37}).
nodes.statement_short: Differentiate the series term by term in $x$, re-index $m\to m+1$ using a Beta contiguous relation, iterate, and repeat the same argument in $y$ and $z$.

nodes.name: Proof of the bounded inequality
nodes.statement:
Setting $z=p/(t(1-t))$, where $t\in(0,1)$ and $\Re(p)>0$, in (ef{ES88}) we obtain \[ \left| K_{
u+ rac{1}{2}}\left( rac{p}{t(1-t)}ight)ight|< rac{1}{2}\left( rac{2|p|t(1-t)}{(\Re (p))^{2}}ight)^{
u+ rac{1}{2}}\Gamma(
u+ s). \] For ease of presentation we shall assume that the parameters $b_j$, $c_j>0$ ($1\leq j\leq 3$). Then, from (ef{PV17}), \[|H_{B,p,
u}(b_1, b_2, b_3;c_1,c_2,c_3;x,y,z)| \leq  rac{\sqrt{2|p|/\pi}}{B(b_1,b_2)}\int_0^1 igg|t^{b_1- rac{3}{2}}(1-t)^{b_2- rac{3}{2}} \,K_{
u+ rac{1}{2}}\left( rac{p}{t(1-t)}ight)\] \[	imes X_4(b_1+b_2,b_3;c_1,c_2,c_3;xt(1-t),y(1-t),zt)  igg|\,dt\] \[< rac{2^
u |p|^{
u+1}}{\sqrt{\pi} (\Re (p))^{2
u+1}}\, rac{\Gamma(
u+ s)}{B(b_1,b_2)} \sum_{m,n,k=0}^\infty  rac{(b_1+b_2)_{2m+n+k} (b_3)_{n+k}}{(c_1)_m(c_2)_n(c_3)_k}\, rac{|x|^m}{m!} rac{|y|^n}{n!} rac{|z|^k}{k!}\] \[\hspace{5cm}	imes\int_0^1t^{b_1+
u+m+k-1}(1-t)^{b_2+
u+m+n-1} dt\]  ee < rac{2^
u |p|^{
u+1}\Gamma(
u+ s)}{\sqrt{\pi} (\Re (p))^{2
u+1}}\,\sum_{m,n,k=0}^\infty  rac{(b_1+b_2)_{2m+n+k}(b_3)_{n+k}}{(c_1)_m(c_2)_n(c_3)_k}\hspace{4.5cm}\] \[\hspace{3cm}	imes rac{B(b_1\!+\!
u\!+\!m\!+\!k,b_2\!+\!
u\!+\!m\!+\!n)}{B(b_1,b_2)}\, rac{|x|^m}{m!} rac{|y|^n}{n!} rac{|z|^k}{k!} \ee which is the result stated in (ef{e51}).
nodes.statement_short: Insert the simplified Bessel bound into the first integral representation and evaluate the remaining Beta integrals termwise.

nodes.name: Proof of the recursion in $b_3$
nodes.statement:
From (ef{PV16}) and the result $ (b_{3}+1)_{n+k}=(b_{3})_{n+k}(1+n/b_{3}+k/b_{3})$, we obtain \[ H_{B,p,
u}(b_{1},b_{2},b_{3}+1;c_{1},c_{2},c_{3};x,y,z)\hspace{7cm}\] \[=\sum_{m,n,k=0}^{\infty} rac{(b_{1}+b_{2})_{2m+n+k}(b_{3}+1)_{n+k}}{(c_{1})_{m}(c_{2})_{n}(c_{3})_{k}} rac{B_{p,
u}(b_{1}+m+k,b_{2}+m+n)} {B(b_{1},b_{2})}  rac{x^{m}}{m!} rac{y^{n}}{n!} rac{z^{k}}{k!}\] \[ =H_{B,p,
u}(b_{1},b_{2},b_{3};c_{1},c_{2},c_{3};x,y,z)\hspace{7cm}\] \[+ rac{y}{b_{3}}\sum_{m=0}^{\infty}\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\sum_{k=0}^{\infty} rac{(b_{1}+b_{2})_{2m+n+k}(b_{3})_{n+k}}{(c_{1})_{m}(c_{2})_{n}(c_{3})_{k}} rac{B_{p,
u}(b_{1}+m+k,b_{2}+m+n)} {B(b_{1},b_{2})}  rac{x^{m}}{m!} rac{y^{n-1}}{(n-1)!} rac{z^{k}}{k!}\]  ee + rac{z}{b_{3}}\sum_{m=0}^{\infty}\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}\sum_{k=1}^{\infty} rac{(b_{1}+b_{2})_{2m+n+k}(b_{3})_{n+k}}{(c_{1})_{m}(c_{2})_{n}(c_{3})_{k}} rac{B_{p,
u}(b_{1}+m+k,b_{2}+m+n)} {B(b_{1},b_{2})}  rac{x^{m}}{m!} rac{y^{n}}{n!} rac{z^{k-1}}{(k-1)!}. \ee Consider the first sum in (ef{e61}) which we denote by $S$. Put $n	o n+1$ and use the identity $(a)_{n+1}=a (a+1)_n$ to find \[S= rac{y}{b_3}\sum_{m,n,k=0}^\infty  rac{(b_1\!+\!b_2)_{2m+n+1+k} (b_3)_{n+1+k}}{(c_1)_m (c_2)_{n+1} (c_3)_k}\,  rac{B_{p,
u}(b_1\!+\!m\!+\!k,b_2\!+\!1\!+\!m\!+\!n)}{B(b_1, b_2)}\, rac{x^m}{m!}  rac{y^{n}}{n!}  rac{z^k}{k!}\] \[= rac{y(b_1\!+\!b_2)}{c_2}\sum_{m,n,k=0}^\infty  rac{(b_1\!+\!b_2\!+\!1)_{2m+n+k} (b_3+1)_{n+k}}{(c_1)_m (c_2+1)_{n} (c_3)_k}\,  rac{B_{p,
u}(b_1\!+\!m\!+\!k,b_2\!+\!1\!+\!m\!+\!n)}{B(b_1, b_2)}\, rac{x^m}{m!}  rac{y^{n}}{n!}  rac{z^k}{k!}.\] Using the fact that $$B(b_1, b_2)= rac{b_1+b_2}{b_2} B(b_1,b_2+1),$$ we then obtain \[S= rac{yb_2}{c_2}\sum_{m,n,k=0}^\infty  rac{(b_1\!+\!b_2\!+\!1)_{2m+n+k} (b_3\!+\!1)_{n+k}}{(c_1)_m (c_2\!+\!1)_{n} (c_3)_k}\,  rac{B_{p,
u}(b_1\!+\!m\!+\!k,b_2\!+\!1\!+\!m\!+\!n)}{B(b_1, b_2+1)}\, rac{x^m}{m!}  rac{y^{n}}{n!}  rac{z^k}{k!}\]  ee = rac{yb_2}{c_2} H_{B,p,
u}(b_1,b_2+1,b_3+1;c_1, c_2+1,c_3; x,y,z). \ee Proceeding in a similar manner for the second series in (ef{e61}) with $k	o k+1$, we find that this sum can be expressed as  ee  rac{zb_1}{c_3} H_{B,p,
u}(b_1+1,b_2,b_3+1;c_1, c_2,c_3+1; x,y,z). \ee Combination of (ef{e62}) and (ef{e63}) with (ef{e61}) then produces the result stated in (ef{e60}).
nodes.statement_short: Split $(b_3+1)_{n+k}$ into three sums, re-index each with $n\to n+1$ and $k\to k+1$, and re-identify them as shifted copies of $H_{B,p,\nu}$.

nodes.name: Proof of the three-term recursion in $c_1$
nodes.statement_short: Expand $(c_1-1)_m$ in terms of $(c_1)_m$, re-index $m\to m+1$, apply the Beta contiguous relation, then replace $c_1$ by $c_1+1$.

nodes.name: Derive the first integral representation from the extended Beta integral
nodes.statement: The proof of the first integral representation (\ref{PV17}) follows by use of the extended beta function (\ref{ES20}) in (\ref{PV16}), a change the order of integration and summation (with uniform convergence of the integral) and, after simplification, use of Exton's triple hypergeometric function (\ref{PV3}), to obtain the right-hand side of the result (\ref{PV17}).
nodes.statement_short: Insert $B_{p,\nu}$ into the series, interchange sum and integral, and recognise Exton's $X_4$.

nodes.name: Obtain the remaining representations by change of variable
nodes.statement: The integral representations (\ref{PV18})-(\ref{PV23}) can be proved directly by using the following transformations \begin{eqnarray*} (\ref{PV18}):\qquad t&=&\frac{(\beta-\gamma)(\xi-\alpha)}{(\beta-\alpha)(\xi-\gamma)},\quad \frac{dt}{d\xi}=\frac{(\beta-\gamma)(\alpha-\gamma)}{(\beta-\alpha) (\xi-\gamma)^2},\\ (\ref{PV20}):\qquad t&=& \sin^2 \xi,\quad \frac{dt}{d\xi}=2\sin \xi \cos \xi\\ (\ref{PV21}):\qquad t&=&\frac{(1+\lambda)\sin^{2}\xi}{1+\lambda \sin^{2}\xi},\quad\frac{dt}{d\xi}=\frac{2(1+\lambda)\sin \xi \cos \xi}{(1+\lambda \sin^2 \xi)^2},\\ (\ref{PV23}):\qquad t&=&\frac{\lambda \sin^{2}\xi}{\cos^2{\xi}+\lambda \sin^{2}\xi},\quad \frac{dt}{d\xi}=\frac{2\lambda \sin \xi \cos \xi}{(\cos^2\xi+\lambda \sin^2\xi)^2}\\ \end{eqnarray*} in turn in (\ref{PV17}) to obtain the right-hand side of each result.
nodes.statement_short: Apply the four listed substitutions $t=t(\xi)$ to the first representation.

nodes.name: Interchange the Mellin integral with the triple sum
nodes.statement: Substituting the extended Srivastava function (\ref{PV16}) into the integral on the left-hand side of (\ref{PV30}) and changing the order of integration (by the uniform convergence of the integral), we obtain \[{\cal M}\left\{H_{B,p,\nu}(b_{1},b_{2},b_{3};c_{1},c_2,c_3;x,y,z)\right\}(s)\hspace{3cm}\] \[=\sum_{m,n,k=0}^{\infty}\frac{(b_{1}+b_{2})_{2m+n+k}(b_{3})_{n+k}}{(c_{1})_{m}(c_{2})_{n}(c_{3})_{k}~B(b_{1},b_{2})}\frac{x^{m}}{m!}\frac{y^{n}}{n!}\frac{z^{k}}{k!} \left\{\int_{0}^{\infty}p^{s-1}B_{p,\nu}(b_{1}+m+k,b_{2}+m+n)\,dp\right\}. \]
nodes.statement_short: Move the $p$-integral inside the series using uniform convergence.

nodes.name: Insert the definition of the extended Beta function
nodes.statement: Using the extended Beta function (\ref{ES20}) then shows that \[{\cal M}\left\{H_{B,p,\nu}(b_{1},b_{2},b_{3};c_{1},c_{2},c_{3};x,y,z)\right\}(s) =\sqrt{\frac{2}{\pi}}\sum_{m,n,k=0}^{\infty}\frac{(b_{1}+b_{2})_{2m+n+k}(b_{3})_{n+k}}{(c_{1})_{m}(c_{2})_{n}(c_{3})_{k}~B(b_{1},b_{2})}\frac{x^{m}}{m!}\frac{y^{n}}{n!}\frac{z^{k}}{k!}\] \[\times\int_{0}^{1}t^{b_{1}+m+k-\frac{3}{2}}(1-t)^{b_{2}+m+n-\frac{3}{2}} \left\{\int_{0}^{\infty}p^{s-\frac{1}{2}}K_{\nu+\frac{1}{2}}\left(\frac{p}{t(1-t)}\right)dp\right\}dt.\]
nodes.statement_short: Replace $B_{p,\nu}$ by its Bessel integral, producing a nested $t$- and $p$-integral.

nodes.name: Evaluate the inner $p$-integral by the Bessel Mellin formula
nodes.statement:
Application of the result \cite[(10.43.19)]{AB26} \[\int_{0}^{\infty}w^{s- rac{1}{2}}K_{\alpha+ rac{1}{2}}(w)dw=2^{s- rac{3}{2}}\Gamma\left( rac{s-\alpha}{2}ight) \Gamma\left( rac{s+\alpha+1}{2}ight)\qquad (|\Re (\alpha)|<\Re (s))\] followed by the substitution $w=p/(t(1-t))$ produces  egin{eqnarray*} {\cal M}\left\{H_{B,p,
u}(b_{1},b_{2},b_{3};c_{1},c_{2},c_{3};x,y,z)ight\}(s) = rac{2^{s-1}}{\sqrt{\pi}}\Gamma\left( rac{s-
u}{2}ight)\Gamma\left( rac{s+
u+1}{2}ight) 
onumber\ 	imes\sum_{m,n,k=0}^{\infty} rac{(b_{1}+b_{2})_{2m+n+k}(b_{3})_{n+k}}{(c_{1})_{m}(c_{2})_{n}(c_{3})_{k}~B(b_{1},b_{2})} rac{x^{m}}{m!} rac{y^{n}}{n!} rac{z^{k}}{k!} \left\{\int_{0}^{1}t^{b_{1}+m+k+s-1}(1-t)^{b_{2}+m+n+s-1}dtight\}. \end{eqnarray*}
nodes.statement_short: Apply the known integral $\int_0^\infty w^{s-1/2}K_{\alpha+1/2}(w)dw$ after substituting $w=p/(t(1-t))$.

nodes.name: Evaluate the remaining $t$-integral as a classical Beta function
nodes.statement:
Evaluation of the integral in terms of the classical Beta function then finally yields  egin{eqnarray*} \Phi(s)={\cal M}\left\{H_{B,p,
u}(b_{1},b_{2},b_{3};c_{1},c_{2},c_{3};x,y,z)ight\}(s) = rac{2^{s-1}}{\sqrt{\pi}}\Gamma\left( rac{s-
u}{2}ight)\Gamma\left( rac{s+
u+1}{2}ight)\ 	imes\sum_{m,n,k=0}^{\infty} rac{(b_{1}+b_{2})_{2m+n+k}(b_{3})_{n+k}}{(c_{1})_{m}(c_{2})_{n}(c_{3})_{k}}  rac{B(b_{1}+m+k+s,b_{2}+m+n+s)}{B(b_{1},b_{2})} rac{x^{m}}{m!} rac{y^{n}}{n!} rac{z^{k}}{k!}. \end{eqnarray*}
nodes.statement_short: Recognise the $t$-integral as $B(b_1+m+k+s, b_2+m+n+s)$.

nodes.name: Identify the resulting sum as $H_B^{(s)}$
nodes.statement: Identifying the above sum as $H_B^{(s)}(b_{1},b_{2},b_{3};c_{1},c_{2},c_{3};x,y,z)$ in (\ref{PV2a}), we obtain the right-hand side of (\ref{PV30}).
nodes.statement_short: Recognise the resummed series as $H_B^{(s)}$, completing the proof.

nodes.name: Differentiate the defining series with respect to $x$
nodes.statement: If we differentiate partially the series for ${\cal H}\equiv H_{B,p,\nu}(b_{1},b_{2},b_{3};c_{1},c_{2},c_{3};x,y,z)$ in (\ref{PV16}) with respect to $x$ we obtain \[\frac{\partial{\cal H}}{\partial x} =\sum_{m=1}^\infty \sum_{n,k=0}^\infty \frac{(b_1+b_2)_{2m+n+k} (b_3)_{n+k}}{(c_1)_m(c_2)_n(c_3)_k}\,\frac{B_{p,\nu}(b_1+m+k,b_2+m+n)}{B(b_1, b_2)}\,\frac{x^{m-1}}{(m-1)!}\frac{y^n}{n!} \frac{z^k}{k!}.\]
nodes.statement_short: Term-by-term $x$-differentiation shifts the summation to $m\ge1$.

nodes.name: Re-index using the Beta contiguous relation and the Pochhammer split
nodes.statement: Making use of the fact that \bee B(b_1,b_2)=\frac{(b_1+b_2)_2}{b_1 b_2}\,B(b_1+1, b_2+1) \ee and $(\lambda)_{m+n}=(\lambda)_m(\lambda+m)_n$, we have upon setting $m \to m+1$ \[\frac{\partial{\cal H}}{\partial x} =\frac{b_1 b_2}{c_1} \sum_{m,n,k=0}^\infty \frac{(b_1+b_2+2)_{2m+n+k} (b_3)_{n+k}}{(c_1+1)_m(c_2)_n(c_3)_k}\,\frac{B_{p,\nu}(b_1\!+\!1\!+\!m\!+\!k,b_2\!+\!1\!+\!m\!+\!n)}{B(b_1+1, b_2+1)}\,\frac{x^{m}}{m!}\frac{y^n}{n!} \frac{z^k}{k!}\] \bee =\frac{b_1 b_2}{c_1}\,H_{B,p,\nu}(b_1+1,b_2+1,b_3;c_1+1,c_2,c_3;x,y,z). \ee
nodes.statement_short: Set $m\to m+1$ and use $B(b_1,b_2)=\frac{(b_1+b_2)_2}{b_1b_2}B(b_1+1,b_2+1)$ to recover $H_{B,p,\nu}$.

nodes.name: Iterate to the $M$-th derivative in $x$
nodes.statement: Repeated application of (\ref{e41}) then yields for $M=1, 2, \ldots $ \[\frac{\partial^M}{\partial x^M}{\cal H}= \frac{(b_1)_M (b_2)_M}{(c_1)_M}\,H_{B,p,\nu}(b_{1}+M,b_{2}+M,b_{3};c_{1}+M,c_{2},c_{3};x,y,z).\]
nodes.statement_short: Repeat the one-step relation $M$ times to get $\partial^M_x{\cal H}$.

nodes.name: Differentiate once with respect to $y$
nodes.statement: A similar reasoning shows that \[\frac{\partial^{M+1}}{\partial x^M \partial y}{\cal H} =\frac{(b_1)_M (b_2)_M}{(c_1)_M} \sum_{m,k=0}^\infty \sum_{n=1}^\infty \frac{(b_1\!+\!b_2\!+\!2M)_{2m+n+k} (b_3)_{n+k}}{(c_1\!+\!M)_m (c_2)_n(c_3)_k}\hspace{3cm}\] \[\hspace{3cm}\times\frac{B_{p, \nu}(b_1\!+\!M\!+\!m\!+\!k,b_2\!+\!M\!+\!n\!+\!k)}{B(b_1\!+\!M, b_2\!+\!M)}\,\frac{x^m}{m!} \frac{y^{n-1}}{(n-1)!}\frac{z^k}{k!}\] \bee =\frac{(b_1)_{M} (b_2)_{M+1} b_3}{(c_1)_{M}c_2}\,H_{B,p,\nu}(b_1+M,b_2+M+1,b_3+1;c_1+M,c_2+1,c_3;x,y,z) \ee upon putting $n\to n+1$ and using the property of the Beta function in (\ref{ES5}).
nodes.statement_short: The same re-indexing in $n$ gives the mixed derivative $\partial^{M+1}_{x^M y}{\cal H}$.

nodes.name: Iterate the $y$-differentiation $N$ times
nodes.statement: Repeated differentiation of (\ref{e42}) $N$ times with respect to $y$ then produces \[\frac{\partial^{M+N}}{\partial x^M \partial y^N} {\cal H}=\frac{(b_1)_M (b_2)_{M+N} (b_3)_N}{(c_1)_M (c_2)_N}\, H_{B,p,\nu}(b_1\!+\!M,b_2\!+\!M\!+\!N,b_3\!+\!N;c_1\!+\!M,c_2\!+\!N,c_3;x,y,z).\]
nodes.statement_short: Repeating in $y$ gives $\partial^{M+N}_{x^My^N}{\cal H}$.

nodes.name: Repeat the argument in $z$ to conclude
nodes.statement: Application of the same procedure to deal with differentiation with respect to $z$ then yields the result stated in (\ref{PV37}).
nodes.statement_short: The identical procedure in $z$ yields the stated formula.

nodes.name: Specialise the Bessel bound to $z=p/(t(1-t))$
nodes.statement_short: Substitute the argument $p/(t(1-t))$ into the simplified Bessel bound.

nodes.name: Bound the integral representation termwise
nodes.statement:
For ease of presentation we shall assume that the parameters $b_j$, $c_j>0$ ($1\leq j\leq 3$). Then, from (ef{PV17}), \[|H_{B,p,
u}(b_1, b_2, b_3;c_1,c_2,c_3;x,y,z)| \leq  rac{\sqrt{2|p|/\pi}}{B(b_1,b_2)}\int_0^1 igg|t^{b_1- rac{3}{2}}(1-t)^{b_2- rac{3}{2}} \,K_{
u+ rac{1}{2}}\left( rac{p}{t(1-t)}ight)\] \[	imes X_4(b_1+b_2,b_3;c_1,c_2,c_3;xt(1-t),y(1-t),zt)  igg|\,dt\] \[< rac{2^
u |p|^{
u+1}}{\sqrt{\pi} (\Re (p))^{2
u+1}}\, rac{\Gamma(
u+ s)}{B(b_1,b_2)} \sum_{m,n,k=0}^\infty  rac{(b_1+b_2)_{2m+n+k} (b_3)_{n+k}}{(c_1)_m(c_2)_n(c_3)_k}\, rac{|x|^m}{m!} rac{|y|^n}{n!} rac{|z|^k}{k!}\] \[\hspace{5cm}	imes\int_0^1t^{b_1+
u+m+k-1}(1-t)^{b_2+
u+m+n-1} dt\]  ee < rac{2^
u |p|^{
u+1}\Gamma(
u+ s)}{\sqrt{\pi} (\Re (p))^{2
u+1}}\,\sum_{m,n,k=0}^\infty  rac{(b_1+b_2)_{2m+n+k}(b_3)_{n+k}}{(c_1)_m(c_2)_n(c_3)_k}\hspace{4.5cm}\] \[\hspace{3cm}	imes rac{B(b_1\!+\!
u\!+\!m\!+\!k,b_2\!+\!
u\!+\!m\!+\!n)}{B(b_1,b_2)}\, rac{|x|^m}{m!} rac{|y|^n}{n!} rac{|z|^k}{k!} \ee
nodes.statement_short: Insert the bound into the first integral representation and evaluate the resulting Beta integrals.

nodes.name: Identify the bound as the stated inequality
nodes.statement: which is the result stated in (\ref{e51}).
nodes.statement_short: Recognise the majorant as $H_B^{(\nu)}$.

nodes.name: Split $(b_3+1)_{n+k}$ into three series
nodes.statement_short: Use $(b_3+1)_{n+k}=(b_3)_{n+k}(1+n/b_3+k/b_3)$ to split the series into three parts.

nodes.name: Re-index the first sum $S$ with $n\to n+1$
nodes.statement_short: Shift $n\to n+1$ and use $(a)_{n+1}=a(a+1)_n$.

nodes.name: Convert $S$ into a shifted $H_{B,p,\nu}$ via a Beta relation
nodes.statement_short: Apply $B(b_1,b_2)=\frac{b_1+b_2}{b_2}B(b_1,b_2+1)$ to recognise $S$ as $\frac{yb_2}{c_2}H_{B,p,\nu}$.

nodes.name: Treat the second sum analogously with $k\to k+1$
nodes.statement: Proceeding in a similar manner for the second series in (\ref{e61}) with $k\to k+1$, we find that this sum can be expressed as \bee \frac{zb_1}{c_3} H_{B,p,\nu}(b_1+1,b_2,b_3+1;c_1, c_2,c_3+1; x,y,z). \ee
nodes.statement_short: The same manipulation in $k$ gives $\frac{zb_1}{c_3}H_{B,p,\nu}$.

nodes.name: Combine the three pieces
nodes.statement: Combination of (\ref{e62}) and (\ref{e63}) with (\ref{e61}) then produces the result stated in (\ref{e60}).
nodes.statement_short: Add the three identified series to obtain the recursion.

nodes.name: Expand $H_{B,p,\nu}$ at $c_1-1$ using $(c_1-1)_m$
nodes.statement_short: Write $(c_1-1)_m=(c_1)_m/\{1+\frac{m}{c_1-1}\}$ and split off the $m\ge1$ remainder.

nodes.name: Re-index the remainder sum with $m\to m+1$
nodes.statement_short: Shift $m\to m+1$ and pull out $(b_1+b_2)_2/(c_1(c_1-1))$.

nodes.name: Apply the Beta contiguous relation to identify the remainder
nodes.statement_short: Use the Beta relation to recognise the remainder as a shifted $H_{B,p,\nu}$.

nodes.name: Shift $c_1\to c_1+1$ to obtain the stated recursion
nodes.statement:
This then yields the recurrence relation (in $c_1$) given by \[H_{B,p,
u}(b_1,b_2,b_3;c_1-1,c_2,c_3;x,y,z)=\] \[H_{B,p,
u}(b_1,b_2,b_3;c_1,c_2,c_3;x,y,z)+ rac{x b_1 b_2}{c_1(c_1-1)} H_{B,p,
u}(b_1+1,b_2+1,b_3;c_1+1,c_2,c_3;x,y,z).\] Replacement of $c_1$ by $c_1+1$ then yields the result stated in (ef{e64}).
nodes.statement_short: Replace $c_1$ by $c_1+1$ in the derived relation.
